area_km2.label: Superficie
area_km2.source_name: Association des Régions du Maroc, 'Indicateurs des régions' ; Ministère de l'Economie et des Finances (DEPF), 'Profils régionaux' (2019)
area_km2.note: UNRESOLVED FOR 9 OF 12 REGIONS. No HCP or Interior-Ministry area table could be opened, and the two published sources that were read disagree. A value is given only where both sources state the same figure (bmk, cs, gon); all others are null. Both sources' figures are kept in 'alternates' so the discrepancy is visible.

association_regions_maroc.note: As displayed on the page. Oriental is shown as the malformed string '8 8681' and is left null here. The page's Laâyoune figure (104 018) is internally consistent with its own density but differs from DEPF.

depf_profils_regionaux_2019.note: Sentences 'superficie de … km2' in each regional chapter. No area sentence found for Fès-Meknès or Souss-Massa. The Drâa-Tafilalet figure (132 167) conflicts with the density quoted in the same chapter (18.6 hab/km2), so it is doubtful.

capitals_source.legal_basis: Décret n° 2.15.40 du 20 février 2015 fixant le nombre des régions, leurs dénominations, leurs chefs-lieux ainsi que les préfectures et provinces qui les composent (Bulletin officiel n° 6340 du 5 mars 2015)
capitals_source.note: Chefs-lieux read in the Wikipedia table that cites the decree (it names the seat prefecture/province: Tanger-Assilah, Oujda-Angad, Fès, Rabat, Béni Mellal, Casablanca, Marrakech, Errachidia, Agadir Ida-Outanane, Guelmim, Laâyoune, Oued Ed-Dahab). The Bulletin officiel text itself was not opened.

unresolved: Employment by sector by region (agriculture / industry / construction / services) and employed population by region: not found. HCP's national note and annual report for 2024 give only rates by region. National figures are filled in; all regional values are null.

Labour-force survey indicators (unemployment, activity, employment rates 2024) are published for the three southern regions as one group 'Régions du Sud' (22.2% unemployment, 45.7% activity, 35.5% employment): Guelmim-Oued Noun, Laâyoune-Sakia El Hamra and Dakhla-Oued Ed-Dahab are null individually. The census unemployment rate is available for each of the 12 regions.

Share of population with higher education by region (RGPH 2024): not collected. It is shown on HCP's interactive platform (resultats2024.rgphapps.ma) but no published document with the 12 regional values was opened. Two published census education measures are supplied instead (share of 25+ with at least collégial level; mean years of schooling). Higher-education student counts by region from the Ministry of Higher Education were not found either.

Chart-only census values, not confirmed by a second reading: illiteracy for Tanger-Tétouan-Al Hoceïma (22.8), Souss-Massa (26.2) and Guelmim-Oued Noun (26.2); census unemployment for Drâa-Tafilalet (22.2) and Marrakech-Safi (20.8); several values of the two education proxies (listed in each indicator's chart_only). They come from bar-chart labels extracted by a PDF parser. In the same document every chart value that is also quoted in the text matched, but in another HCP PDF (regional accounts 2024) the parser misread small-bar labels, so these should be checked by eye against the PDF before publication.

The RGPH 2024 results note was read in a copy hosted by casainvest.ma (Centre Régional d'Investissement de Casablanca-Settat), not on hcp.ma. The HCP file https://www.hcp.ma/file/242665/ appears to be the related HCP document but was not opened to confirm it is identical.

Area (km2): unresolved for 9 of 12 regions. The Association des Régions du Maroc page and the Finance Ministry's 'Profils régionaux' disagree (e.g. Tanger-Tétouan-Al Hoceïma 17 262 vs 16 679; Laâyoune-Sakia El Hamra 104 018 vs 138 666; Dakhla-Oued Ed-Dahab 130 898 vs 142 865), and each contains an obvious internal error. The Interior Ministry document 'Les régions du Maroc en chiffres' (collectivites-territoriales.gov.ma) would be the natural authority but failed to load. Only the three figures on which both sources agree are filled in.
Regional capitals were read in Wikipedia's table citing Décret n° 2.15.40; the decree text itself was not opened.

GDP: the latest HCP release is the 2024 regional accounts (July 2026), newer than the 2023 release the brief expected. Both years are supplied. The 2023 values are the revised ones from the 2024 release; the first-release 2023 values are kept under gdp_2023_mad_million.first_release. Regional GDP sums to the national total only after adding the 'enclaves extra-territoriales' line (1 471 MAD million in 2024, 1 452 in 2023), which HCP does not allocate to any region; residual differences of a few MAD million are rounding.

In the 2023 regional-accounts note the GDP-per-capita chart swaps the labels of Oriental and Béni Mellal-Khénifra relative to its own annex table; the annex table was followed. Not relevant to the revised figures used here, but worth knowing if that note is cited.
HCP's GDP per capita uses its own population denominator, so it will not equal regional GDP divided by the census population.
Unemployment for 2025 (HCP 'Activité, emploi et chômage, résultats annuels 2025') exists but was not collected; the brief asked for 2024.
Monetary poverty by region is from the 2022 survey (ENNVM); no newer regional monetary poverty rate was found.
